s: 36 km² desert reserve north-east of Doha · a brake on urban spread
te: Open desert kept free for nature
se: North of Doha’s new city, Al Wusail keeps 36 km² of open desert for plants and animals
sa: شمال المدينة الجديدة في الدوحة تحفظ الوسيل 36 كيلومترًا مربعًا من الصحراء المفتوحة للنباتات والحيوانات
desc: Al Wusail Reserve covers about 36 km² north-east of Doha on Qatar’s east coast and was founded under Law No. 7 of 2005. Qatar e-Nature says it was chosen to meet biodiversity strategy goals and to limit rapid urbanisation, and notes distinctive geological features and historical value. Al Daayen’s development strategy describes large parts of the municipality’s central east as the Al Wusail Environmental Protected Area.
sig: Keeps an open stretch of east-coast desert protected next to one of Qatar’s fastest-growing urban areas.
disc: Set up partly to limit urban sprawl
refs: Qatar News Agency (15 April 2025). Qatar’s nature reserves promoting ecosystem sustainability and wildlife preservation. https://qna.org.qa/en/News-Area/News/2025-4/15/qatar-s-nature-reserves-promoting-ecosystem-sustainability-and-wildlife-preservation
Wikipedia. Al Daayen (citing Ministry of Municipality and Environment, Al Daayen Municipality: Vision and Development Strategy, 2017). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Daayen
conf: Coordinates are the GeoNames point for the locality Al Wusayl (alternate name Lusail), Al Daayen, which gives the reserve its name, ≈5 km; no official boundary was found. International Parks gives 25.35, 51.55, which falls on the Lusail–Pearl coast and was not used. QNA’s English text calls it ‘Lusail’ Reserve with the same 36 km² and law

s: Meadow reserve of north-east Qatar · verdant rawdat and dense vegetation
dr: Listed among Qatar’s 12 nature reserves (2014 data)
se: Around Umm Qarn, green rain-fed meadows with thick plant cover are protected as a nature reserve
sa: حول أم قرن تُحمى مروج خضراء تغذيها الأمطار ويغطيها نبات كثيف
desc: Umm Qarn Reserve lies about 25 km from Doha in north-eastern Qatar. Qatar e-Nature and QNA describe it as rich in meadows (rawdat) with verdant spots and dense vegetation. It was one of the 12 nature reserves counted in Qatar’s 2014 statistics; no area or founding law is published.
sig: Protects part of the rawda meadows that hold most of Qatar’s inland plant cover.
refs: Qatar News Agency (15 April 2025). Qatar’s nature reserves promoting ecosystem sustainability and wildlife preservation. https://qna.org.qa/en/News-Area/News/2025-4/15/qatar-s-nature-reserves-promoting-ecosystem-sustainability-and-wildlife-preservation
The Peninsula (26 February 2016). 23% of land under natural reserves. https://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/26/02/2016/23-of-land-under-natural-reserves
conf: Coordinates are the Wikipedia infobox point for the village of Umm Qarn, Al Daayen (25°34′40″N 51°27′0″E), after which the reserve is named; no source states where the reserve lies relative to the village, ≈5 km. No designation year found; timeline start is the 2014 listing

s: Small biodiversity reserve north of Umm Al Amad · shield against urban sprawl
dr: Listed among Qatar’s 12 nature reserves (2014 data)
se: Just north of the village of Umm Al Amad, a small piece of desert is protected because so many living things share it
sa: شمال قرية أم العمد مباشرة تُحمى قطعة صغيرة من الصحراء لأن كثيرًا من الكائنات الحية تتقاسمها
desc: Sunai Reserve lies north-west of Doha and, according to Umm Salal municipality’s development strategy, covers about 4 km² immediately north of the village of Umm Al Amad. Qatar e-Nature and QNA say it was designated for its high biodiversity and to guard against urban sprawl. It is one of three protected environmental areas in Umm Salal municipality.
sig: A small protected patch of rawda landscape in a fast-developing municipality.
disc: Immediately north of Umm Al Amad
refs: Qatar News Agency (15 April 2025). Qatar’s nature reserves promoting ecosystem sustainability and wildlife preservation. https://qna.org.qa/en/News-Area/News/2025-4/15/qatar-s-nature-reserves-promoting-ecosystem-sustainability-and-wildlife-preservation

Wikipedia. Umm Al Amad (Qatar) (citing Ministry of Municipality and Environment, Umm Slal Municipality: Vision and Development Strategy, 2017, p. 27). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umm_Al_Amad_(Qatar)
conf: Coordinates are the Wikipedia infobox point for the village of Umm Al Amad (25°29′32″N 51°24′1″E); the reserve lies immediately north of it, ≈2 km. Region is Umm Salal per the municipal strategy, not Al Shahaniya as in the task list. Area from the municipal strategy via Wikipedia. Arabic spelling from the task list, not verified (Al Sanee in some English sources). No designation year found; timeline start is the 2014 listing

s: West-coast sabkha where microbial mats help make dolomite · Holocene
dr: Holocene evaporitic sabkha with living microbial mats
el: About 109 Mg of carbon per hectare
se: On Qatar’s west coast, slimy mats of microbes in a salt flat help grow dolomite, a rock that is hard to make anywhere else today
sa: على الساحل الغربي لقطر تساعد حُصُر لزجة من الميكروبات في سبخة ملحية على تكوين الدولوميت، وهو صخر يصعب أن يتكوّن في أي مكان آخر اليوم
desc: Dohat Faishakh is a coastal sabkha on the north-west coast of the Qatar peninsula whose sediments, dominated by gypsum and carbonate minerals, formed during the Holocene and are covered with microbial mats. Cores DF1–DF4 showed that dolomite forms not only in the evaporitic supratidal zone but also within microbial mats in the lower intertidal zone, closely tied to the mats’ extracellular polymeric substances, pointing to a microbially influenced process. Porewater salinity ranged from 140 to 310‰, and sediment carbon stocks averaged about 109.1 ± 7.1 Mg C per hectare, higher than at Khor Al Adaid sabkha (67.8) and above the soil carbon of Qatari mangroves.
sig: A natural laboratory for how dolomite, a major reservoir rock of the Arabian Gulf region, can form at low temperature with the help of microbes.
ex: Brauchli et al. (2016); Al Disi et al. (2023)
refs: Brauchli, M., McKenzie, J.A., Strohmenger, C.J., Sadooni, F., Vasconcelos, C. & Bontognali, T.R.R. (2016). The importance of microbial mats for dolomite formation in the Dohat Faishakh sabkha, Qatar. Carbonates and Evaporites 31, 339–345. https://doi.org/10.1007/s13146-015-0275-0

Al Disi, Z.A., Naja, K., Rajendran, S., Elsayed, H., Strakhov, I., Al Saad Al-Kuwari, H., Sadooni, F., Dittrich, M. & Al-Khayat, J.A. (2023). Variability of blue carbon storage in arid evaporitic environment of two coastal Sabkhas or mudflats. Scientific Reports 13, 12723. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-39762-7
conf: Coordinates are the published sampling point (Al Disi et al. 2023, Table 1: 25°38′8.17″N 50°57′36.48″E); Brauchli et al. cores lie within about 1.5 km. Timeline span is a broad estimate: the sabkha is dated only as Holocene. Region assigned by nearest municipality (Al Shahaniya); the sources give none. Arabic name is a transliteration made for this record

n: Fahahil reference section (Rus and Dammam formations)
na: المقطع المرجعي لتكويني الرس والدمام في الفحاحيل
s: Cliffs near Dukhan that serve as Qatar’s reference section for its Eocene rocks
el: About 26 m of exposed Rus Formation
se: In low cliffs near Dukhan, layers of limestone, marl and shale record the warm shallow sea that covered Qatar about 50 million years ago
sa: في جروف منخفضة قرب دخان تسجّل طبقات الحجر الجيري والمارل والطَّفل البحر الدافئ الضحل الذي غطّى قطر قبل نحو 50 مليون عام
desc: Cliffs about 1 km east of the Fahahil plant near Dukhan form the Qatar reference section described by Cavelier (1970) for the country’s surface Eocene rocks. About 26 m of the Rus Formation is exposed: whitish, soft, variably dolomitised limestone and green to brown dolomitic marl, with chert and quartz geodes near the base. Above it the section shows the base of the Dammam Formation, with the full Alveolina Bed, the Midra Shale Member and the bottom of the Umm Bab Member. The Rus is Early Eocene (Ypresian, about 56–48.9 Ma) and the Dammam Early to Middle Eocene, ending about 41.4 Ma.
sig: The standard surface section against which Qatar’s two main Eocene formations, also its main aquifer rocks, are described.
refs: LeBlanc, J. (2021). Stratigraphic Lexicon: A revised guide to the Cenozoic surface formations of Qatar, Middle East (excluding the islands). BIOSIS: Biological Systems. https://doi.org/10.37819/biosis.001.04.0134 (entries Rus Fm, https://qatarlex.geolex.org/formations/Rus%20Fm, and Dammam Fm, https://qatarlex.geolex.org/formations/Dammam%20Fm)
Sadooni, F.N. (2014). Geology of Qatar (booklet). Environmental Studies Center, Qatar University. https://home.qu.edu.qa/en-us/Research/esc/Documents/Books/booklets/Geology_of_Qatar.pdf
conf: Coordinates as published in the lexicon for the reference section (25°17′15.79″N 50°48′12.60″E). Cavelier (1970) is cited through LeBlanc (2021), not read directly. About 15 km from the existing Dukhan Anticline record, a different feature. Region assigned by nearest municipality (Al Shahaniya). Arabic name made for this record
